key_insight: LLM judgments of solid-state synthesis recipes were driven mainly by thermal features, with reaction chemistry modulating their effect.
engineering_relevance: LLMs may provide a thermally informed prior for prioritizing synthesis recipes, but their rankings still require experimental validation.
method: Benchmark 240 synthesis experiments across eight known and unknown inorganic oxides.
Use GPT-5.6-Sol to compare recipe pairs, then aggregate preferences with a regularized Bradley–Terry model.
Evaluate rankings against X-ray diffraction purity measurements and selectively withhold recipe information.
evidence_signal: Pairwise accuracy was 0.72 overall; on six thermally driven targets, accuracy was 0.68 without chemical identity versus 0.56 without temperature.
watch_item: Results cover fixed recipe banks for only eight oxides and do not establish reliable generation of new synthesis recipes.
paper_title: What Do LLMs Use to Judge Synthesis Recipes? An Experimental Analysis on 240 Solid-State Syntheses
